correctness.rationale: Graded copy invariance forces equal 2×2 diagonal blocks aJ_f and equal off-diagonal blocks yJ_f; antisymmetry gives this form even for the covariance of a physical non-Gaussian extension. The copy-space eigenvalues are u=a+(n−1)y and v=a−y. Covariance feasibility gives |u|,|v|≤1, and conversely every pair in this square gives an invariant Gaussian extension with the specified Gaussian marginal. Rotating the two retained copies on both Majorana coordinates has determinant +1 and leaves the product covariance invariant; it turns the correlated covariance into one-mode sectors a+y and a−y. The two operators are now diagonal in the same occupation basis. Writing h=(u−v)/(2n), differences of their probabilities are −h², −h², h+h², −h+h². Since |h|≤1/n≤1/2, their absolute sum is 2|h|+2h², increasing strictly in |h|. Thus only opposite endpoints u,v=±1 attain 2/n+2/n², including n=2. Equivalently, a uniform single-particle Slater state, or its particle-hole partner, realizes an equality extension. The value is the full Schatten norm, not half that norm.
residual_risks: The optional rational grid is corroboration only. The proof uses the exact sector square and even Gaussian determination by covariance, not a finite grid.

evidence: The anchor covers the identical symmetry and target broadly, giving 4/n for this specialization. Negari–Salek optimize a distance to the separable set under two-sided extendibility. broader_coverage.reasoning: The anchor's upper bound is strictly larger for every n≥2. Bounds to an approximating set or mixture do not give a sharp bound to the single prescribed marginal product, even where symmetries are related.

evidence: The two-sector feasibility criterion and a sharp covariance corner are prior. The general mixed-state inequality gives at most half the Schatten norm of the covariance difference and, used here, yields the known loose 4/n state bound.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The corner in the previous paper supplies a candidate, but a maximizer of covariance norm need not generally maximize state norm. Simultaneous diagonalization at the two-copy marginal and the cancellation of its mean parameter in the exact trace norm prove the needed global monotonicity and equality classification.

checked_sources: arXiv:2610.01860v1, Theorem IV.2 and Remark IV.5
value.rationale: One mode and two retained copies are the first nontrivial instance of this motivated de Finetti distance; one retained copy always has zero error. The exact result identifies which part of the general bound is slack even at a sharp covariance configuration, with an asymptotic factor-of-two gap and equality information for every extension length. It provides a useful benchmark for sharper state-level conversions rather than a numerical re-evaluation of the old covariance optimum.
residual_risks: No inference to multi-mode or larger retained marginals, non-Gaussian marginals, or optimal product-mixture approximation.
